issues.description: The Meal constructor parameter order in the template does not match the problem specification (and the solution). The UML and problem text specify Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), and the solution implements this order. However, the template's Meal constructor is declared as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This mismatch will cause compilation errors or confusion when students try to use the provided Main examples and follow the UML, preventing them from implementing the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Meal constructor signature to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) so parameter order matches the UML/problem description and the solution. Update constructor parameter names accordingly and ensure example usages in Main (new Meal("name", new String[]{...})) compile.

issues.description: The problem statement's UML and the solution expect Meal constructor signature Meal(String, String[]), i.e., name first then ingredients. The template repository's Meal.java defines the constructor with the parameters reversed (Meal(String[] ingredients, String name)). This signature mismatch forces students to reconcile differing constructor orders across artifacts, will cause compilation confusion when following examples in Main, and obscures the direct mapping from the problem specification to the template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java to public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) so the parameter order (name, ingredients) matches the problem statement and the solution. Update any call sites if needed.
